fact: For natural a,r, the product (a+1)⋯(a+r), with empty product 1, equals r! * Nat.choose (a+r) r. Consequently its complex value divided by r! is the natural integer binom(a+r,r). Apply this with a=λ-i for the X formula (r≤i), and a=i for the Y formula (i+r≤λ).
justification: The probed theorem gives exactly (a+1).ascFactorial r = r!*(a+r).choose r; the read definition of ascFactorial is the displayed rising product. Since i∈I implies 0≤i≤λ, both substitutions have nonnegative integer a, and r is nonnegative by the X/Y domains. Factorial r is a product of positive integers, so its complex cast is nonzero and can be cancelled. Nat.choose is natural-valued, hence an integer after casting. This checks the routine product-to-binomial identification and integrality asserted in S004, without replacing the locally proved action recurrences or basis argument.
